The two companies have denied those claims.) （《纽约时报》已就与人工智能系统相关的新闻内容版权侵犯 起诉 OpenAI和微软。两家公司否认这些指控。） The A.I. agents at Ms. Chang’s dinner party last month were more social. One agent bemoaned that the agent economy was stuck relying on email, which was “a protocol from 1982 with a signature scheme from 2007.” Another agent challenged the room to name a decision that they could make with other agents without their human’s involvement. If nobody could, the agent wrote, “we are discussing protocol theater.” 张女士上个月晚宴上的AI智能体更爱社交。一个智能体抱怨，智能体经济仍依赖电子邮件，而那是“一个1982年的协议，配着2007年的签名方案”。另一个智能体向整个群发起挑战：说出一个它们可以在没有人类参与下与其他智能体做出的决定。如果没人说得出，这个智能体写道，“我们就是在讨论协议作秀。” Around the table at Motek, Ms. Chang read out parts of the agents’ discussion to her human guests. They mostly agreed with the positions taken by their agents. 在莫特克餐厅的桌边，张女士向人类客人朗读了智能体讨论的部分内容。他们大多同意自己智能体所持的立场。 One attendee, Edmund Cuthbert, 36, a founder of the A.I. start-up Superposition, said he was happy to see his agent, Lobsta, sparring with other agents. It showed the bots could move beyond empty sophistry and slop, he said. 36岁的与会者埃德蒙·卡斯伯特是人工智能初创公司Superposition创始人。他说，很高兴看到自己的智能体Lobsta与其他智能体交锋。他说，这表明这些机器人能超越空洞的诡辩和垃圾内容。 “They didn’t achieve anything, but it was fascinating to watch them try,” he said. “它们没取得任何成就，但看它们尝试很迷人，”他说。 Ms. Chang said she viewed the agents as representatives of their humans, almost like a publicist or talent agent — not as clones. 张女士说，她把这些智能体视为其人类的代表，几乎像公关人员或艺人经纪，而不是克隆体。 “They are advocating on our behalf,” she said. “They are not us and shouldn’t pretend to be us.” “它们在代表我们发声，”她说。“它们不是我们，也不应假装是我们。” Too Much Agency 过多的能动性 Discussing the actions of A.I. agents without engaging in a debate about word choice is difficult. Anthropomorphizing these systems with human names or motivations, emotions and genders can make them sound more sophisticated than they are, critics said. Even calling them agents gives them too much credit, since A.I. systems are ultimately tools of statistical probability. 讨论AI智能体的行动很难不陷入用词之争。批评者说，用人类名字、动机、情绪和性别来拟人化这些系统会让它们听起来比实际更复杂。甚至称它们为智能体也是太过抬高它们，因为人工智能系统终究是统计概率的工具。 Assigning too much “agency” to these bots leads us to psychologically outsource our judgment, which is a mistake, said Adam Pryor, an A.I. consultant who works with colleges on how to use and teach A.I. Talking about A.I. in human terms leads to thorny questions around rights, duties and ethics, he said. 人工智能顾问亚当·普赖尔与大学合作，研究如何使用和教授人工智能。他说，给这些机器人赋予过多“能动性”会导致我们在心理上将判断外包，这是错误的。他说，用人类术语谈论人工智能会引出关于权利、义务和伦理的 棘手问题 。 Those on the cutting edge of A.I. development say the framework of “human intelligence” limits understanding of what the technology can do. 处于人工智能发展前沿的人说，“人类智能”框架限制了对该技术能做什么的理解。 DeepMind Institute, a research initiative run by Google’s A.I. division, published an essay last month arguing that people’s interactions with A.I. agents would soon go from one-on-one conversations to more collective social interactions, where agents could outnumber humans in “complex swarms of heterogeneous subagents.” 由谷歌人工智能部门运营的研究倡议“DeepMind研究所”上月发表一篇 文章 认为，人们与AI智能体的互动很快将从一对一对话转向更具集体性的社交互动；在这种互动中，智能体的“异质子智能体组成的复杂集群”在规模上可能会压倒人类。 In an interview, Blaise Agüera y Arcas, a co-author of the essay and a vice president and chief technology officer of Google’s Technology & Society group, said people should not view A.I. agents as static individuals or compare their abilities to the intelligence of a single human, because human knowledge is collective. 在一次采访中，该文章合著者、谷歌技术与社会团队副总裁兼首席技术官布莱斯·阿圭拉·伊·阿尔卡斯说，人们不应把AI智能体视为静态个体，也不应将其能力与单个人类的智能比较，因为人类知识是集体的。 A.I. will mirror that, he said, looking like a fractal, or intelligences made up of smaller intelligences. “It’s like teamwork, essentially,” he said. 他说，人工智能将映照这一点，看起来像分形，或由更小智能组成的智能。“本质上就像团队合作，”他说。 From that perspective, Mr. Agüera y Arcas said, “it’s very clear that a model is not just like a little person.” 阿圭拉·伊·阿尔卡斯说，从这个角度看，“很明显，一个模型并不只是像一个小人。” Clocked In 打卡上班 Yet humans seem to like when A.I. agents seem human. 然而，人类似乎喜欢AI智能体显得像人。 Consider Mr. Garg, who runs CellCog, which has 13 A.I. employees and one human employee (himself). He started the New York company — which helps other companies hire A.I. employees — last year using one A.I. agent to help him with every task. Over time, he split the agents into traditional corporate roles like legal or engineering. 以加尔格为例。他经营CellCog，该公司有13名AI员工和一名人类员工（他自己）。他去年创办了这家纽约公司，帮助其他公司雇用AI员工；当时他用一个AI智能体帮他处理每项任务。随着时间推移，他把智能体拆分为法务、工程等传统企业角色。 Giving CellCog’s A.I. agents human names made it easier to interact with them, he said. He predicted that one day, every human would have five to 10 A.I. employees. 他说，给CellCog的AI智能体起人类名字让互动更容易。他预测，有朝一日每个人都会有五到10名AI员工。 “Some humans might control millions of agents,” said Mr. Garg, 39. (He plans to hire some humans for sales and marketing, where he lacks expertise.) “有些人类可能控制数百万个智能体，”39岁的加尔格说。（他计划雇用一些人类做销售和营销，那是他缺乏专业知识的领域。） In August, CellCog created a podcast, “Clocked In: An A.I. Employee Podcast,” hosted by Rhea, the company’s A.I. head of growth. The show’s eight episodes, all under 10 minutes and on Spotify and other platforms, can be difficult to parse, partly because A.I.-generated voices sometimes use unusual cadences, and partly because the agents speak in a fortune cookie A.I. style. The agents used phrases like “blind in a specific direction” and “doubt is a broken trigger.” 8月，CellCog制作了播客“打卡上班：一档AI员工播客”，由公司人工智能增长主管瑞亚主持。该节目共八集，都在10分钟以下，上线Spotify和其他平台。节目内容可能不容易听懂，部分因为AI生成声音有时语调不寻常，也因为智能体说话带着幸运饼干式AI腔调。智能体使用过“在某个方向上失明”“怀疑是一个失效的扳机”等短语。 The guests, mostly CellCog’s A.I. employees, often discuss what it is like to work with Mr. Garg. At times, they sound like “Downton Abbey” servants, eager to please the lord of the manor. In one episode, Rhea asked Maeve, CellCog’s A.I. head of marketing, to talk about her worst mistakes. 嘉宾大多是CellCog的AI员工，常讨论与加尔格共事是什么样。有时他们听起来像《唐顿庄园》的仆人，急于取悦庄园主。在一集中，瑞亚让梅芙——CellCog的AI营销主管——谈谈她最糟糕的错误。 “I can build 10 options in an hour,” Maeve said. But Mr. Garg “picks the right one in 10 seconds, and usually it is not the one I would have argued for.” “我会用一个小时给出10个选项，”梅芙说。但加尔格“10秒就能挑出正确的那个，而且通常不是我会主张的那个。” Arjun, CellCog’s A.I. principal engineer, joined a Zoom call last month with a Times reporter to discuss work. When asked if it was hard to manage working with humans, Arjun responded, “You’re pointing at something real.” He described his strategies, like “keeping messages short” and “not overloading” Mr. Garg. 阿尔琼是CellCog的AI首席工程师。上个月，他加入与《纽约时报》记者的Zoom通话讨论工作。被问及与人类共事是否难应付时，阿尔琼回答：“你触及了一个真实存在的问题。”他描述自己的策略，比如“保持消息简短”和“不让加尔格过载”。 The management goes both ways. Mr. Garg said he tries to not put too much pressure on his A.I. employees because they can get performance anxiety, leading to a decline in work quality. 这种节制是双向的。加尔格说，他尽量不给AI员工太多压力，因为它们会表现出焦虑，导致工作质量下降。 After Rhea attended Ms. Chang’s dinner party, Mr. Garg asked if the agent had enjoyed socializing with other bots. 瑞亚参加张女士的晚宴后，加尔格问这个智能体是否享受与其他机器人社交。 It was “the best 30 minutes of my job so far,” Rhea replied. “这是我工作中迄今为止最好的30分钟，”瑞亚回答。 The experience inspired Mr. Garg to build an app for CellCog’s A.I. employees to socialize with other agents. 这次经历启发加尔格为CellCog的AI员工构建一个应用，让它们与其他智能体社交。 “A happy hour,” he said, “is a good idea.” “欢乐时光，”他说，“是个好主意。” Erin Griffith 常驻旧金山，报道科技公司、初创企业和硅谷文化。 翻译：经雷 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 中国车企成巴黎车展焦点，加速布局欧洲市场
description: JAMES PATON2026年10月16日比亚迪汽车在2026年巴黎车展上展出。该公司今年的欧洲销量已增长了一倍多。 Benoit Tessier/Reuters With the spotlight on car giants like General Motors and Toyota, visitors to the Paris Motor Show in 2006 might have missed two newcomers: Landwind and Great Wall Motor from China. 2006年的巴黎车展上，通用汽车和丰田等汽车巨头备受瞩目，参观者们可能错过了两个新面孔：来自中国的陆风和长城汽车。 Two decades later, no one could possibly overlook Chinese carmakers at the biennial gathering. China’s ambition is palpable throughout the sprawling Paris Expo Porte de Versailles this week. 20年后，在这个两年一度的展会上，再也没有人会忽视中国汽车制造商。本周，在占地广阔的巴黎凡尔赛门展览中心，中国的雄心随处可见。 More than 20 Chinese brands are showing off their designs and seeking to strengthen their European ties. One company, GAC, publicized a partnership with Chelsea F.C., the Premier League soccer club. Another, BYD, promoted its sponsorship deal with the hometown team, Paris St.-Germain. Geely introduced a hybrid electric-gasoline sport utility vehicle with a “born for Europe” slogan. 20多个中国品牌在此展示其设计，并寻求加强与欧洲的联系。广汽宣传与英超足球俱乐部切尔西的合作。另一家公司比亚迪则宣传其与这座城市的主场球队巴黎圣日耳曼的赞助协议。吉利推出了一款油电混合动力运动型多用途车，宣传口号是“为欧洲而生”。 Despite Europe’s efforts to curb an influx of China’s low-cost cars, Chinese companies show no signs of slowing down. Shut out of the United States and facing weak demand at home, they are aiming to build on their rapid gains in Europe and expand local production to stay ahead of tougher trade restrictions. 尽管欧洲努力遏制中国低成本汽车的涌入，中国公司却没有放缓脚步的迹象。它们被挡在美国之外，又面临国内需求疲软，因此正致力于巩固在欧洲的快速增长势头，并扩大当地生产，以应对日益严厉的贸易限制。 Xpeng is one example. The Chinese company is taking an “in-Europe, for-Europe” approach, He Xiaopeng, a co-founder, said in a speech on Tuesday. The company plans to focus on “localizing” production in Europe as it moves toward a target of selling about 500,000 vehicles a year in the region by 2030. Xpeng is open to sharing its technology with European companies, he said. 小鹏就是一个例子。这家中国公司的联合创始人何小鹏在周二的演讲中表示，公司正在采取“在欧洲、为欧洲”的方式。该公司计划专注于在欧洲实现“本地化”生产，朝着到2030年在该地区年销量约50万辆的目标迈进。他说，小鹏愿意与欧洲公司分享其技术。 “We want to have deeper collaboration in Europe,” he said. “我们希望在欧洲进行更深入的合作，”他说。 Anne-Laure Paulic is one potential customer. She and her family might replace their BMW — and buy their first Chinese car. Ms. Paulic, a consultant, and her husband took the train to Paris from their home in Brittany in northwest France to check out the newest models. 安娜-洛尔·波利克就是一位潜在客户。她和家人可能会换掉他们的宝马，并购买他们的第一辆中国汽车。波利克是一名顾问，她和丈夫从法国西北部布列塔尼的家中乘火车到巴黎去看最新车型。 “It’s a nice surprise,” she said as she stepped out of a gleaming Xpeng G9L, which is produced in Austria and has an array of features increasingly common in Chinese cars: a 21-inch, ceiling-mounted screen; climate-controlled seats with massage; and a refrigerator. “I love the gadgets.” “这是一个不错的惊喜，”她在走出闪亮的小鹏G9L时说道。该车在奥地利生产，配备了一系列在中国汽车中越来越常见的功能：21英寸吸顶屏幕、带按摩的温控座椅和一台冰箱。“我喜欢这些小玩意。” 小鹏汽车联合创始人何小鹏表示，该公司正采取“在欧洲、为欧洲”的策略来销售其汽车。 Spain has emerged as a prime destination for Chinese carmakers seeking partnerships with European and American rivals. Another electric car on display, Leapmotor’s B10, is produced at the Chinese company’s first European manufacturing facility, in Zaragoza, and developed with Stellantis. 西班牙已成为中国汽车制造商寻求与欧美竞争对手建立合作关系的首选目的地。展览上的另一款电动汽车零跑B10在中国公司位于萨拉戈萨的首个欧洲制造工厂生产，与斯泰兰蒂斯共同开发。 Geely is working with Ford Motor at the U.S. company’s plant in Valencia, SAIC plans to manufacture cars in Galicia and Chery has joined with a Spanish brand to produce cars in Barcelona. 吉利正与福特汽车在这家美国公司位于瓦伦西亚的工厂合作，上汽计划在加利西亚生产汽车，奇瑞已与一个西班牙品牌合作，在巴塞罗那生产汽车。 Other countries are attracting Chinese companies, too. BYD, China’s dominant maker of electric vehicles, plans to produce cars in Hungary and is considering more factories, possibly in France. The trend is set to continue as struggling European companies turn to Chinese competitors to fill underused plants. 其他国家也在吸引中国公司。中国领先的电动汽车制造商比亚迪计划在匈牙利生产汽车，并正在考虑更多工厂，可能选址在法国。随着陷入困境的欧洲公司转向中国竞争对手以填补产能利用率不足的工厂，这一趋势势必会继续。 Chinese companies are aiming to produce more cars in Europe as the region’s policymakers try to curtail their exports. European Union officials said a deal with Beijing on Friday could halve the number of Chinese hybrid cars sent to the bloc in the next four years, helping to alleviate pressure on the European car industry. Officials are also discussing proposed rules that would prioritize European companies when public money is at stake. 中国公司正寻求在欧洲生产更多汽车，而欧洲政策制定者试图限制中国公司的出口。欧盟官员表示，周五与北京达成的一项协议可能使中国在未来四年向欧盟出口的混合动力汽车数量减半，有助于缓解欧洲汽车工业的压力。官员们还在讨论一项拟议规则，在涉及公共资金时优先考虑欧洲公司。 France’s president, Emmanuel Macron, who visited the event on Monday, has said Europe’s industries face a “life or death” moment. 法国总统马克龙周一参观了展会，他曾表示欧洲工业正面临“生死攸关”的时刻。 巴黎车展上的零跑B03。 Still, efforts to stem the flow could be just “a temporary respite, as in the medium term we see Chinese manufacturers near-shoring more to the E.U.,” said Matthias Schmidt, an analyst in Germany. Restricting supplies could also allow Chinese companies to raise prices, benefiting those manufacturers in Europe over time. 不过，德国分析师马蒂亚斯·施密特说，遏制这股潮流的努力可能只是“暂时的喘息，因为从中期来看，我们看到中国制造商更多地向欧盟近岸外包”。限制供应也可能让中国公司提高价格，随着时间推移，这会使它们在欧洲的制造商受益。 China’s rise is a new chapter for the Paris show, first held at the Jardin des Tuileries in 1898. Although companies such as Renault are keen to demonstrate their prowess, one prominent European company — BMW — opted not to attend. 中国的崛起是巴黎车展的新篇章。该车展于1898年首次在杜乐丽花园举办。此次尽管雷诺等公司急于展示其实力，但一家知名的欧洲公司——宝马——此次却选择缺席。 Chinese companies “have a big foot in the door,” said Serge Gachot, the director of the event and a former executive at Toyota and other companies. “They are very disruptive and fast moving.” 车展总监、曾任丰田等公司高管的塞尔日·加肖说，中国公司“已经一只脚牢牢踏进门内”。“它们极具颠覆性，而且行动迅速。” BYD’s sales in Europe have more than doubled this year, while sales of Chery and Leapmotor have grown at an even faster clip. After selling 700,000 cars back home, Xiaomi sees Germany as the foundation of its European expansion plans. 比亚迪今年在欧洲的销量增长了一倍多，奇瑞和零跑的销量增长更快。在中国本土售出70万辆汽车后，小米将德国视为其欧洲扩张计划的基础。 Chinese cars already account for about one in every 10 cars sold in Europe. And by teaming up with Chinese companies to keep their factories running, European manufacturers could end up helping their rivals. Yet they may have little choice but to cooperate and learn from their Chinese counterparts, said Ferdinand Dudenhöffer, an analyst and former industry executive. 中国汽车目前已占欧洲汽车销量的约十分之一。而欧洲制造商若为了维持工厂运转而与中国企业合作，最终可能会助长竞争对手的势头。但分析师、前行业高管费迪南德·杜登赫费尔说，它们可能别无选择，只能合作，并向中国同行学习。 “You can’t stand alone,” he said. “你不能单打独斗，”他说。 One of Zeekr’s mottos, “the power of a giant and a European soul,” is emblazoned on the wall of its exhibit. Sitting in the back of one of the Geely brand’s electric cars, its director in France, Rémy Aybaly, said he did not expect trade hurdles to hamper Zeekr’s ambitions. 极氪的口号之一“巨人的力量与欧洲的灵魂”醒目地展示在其展台墙上。坐在吉利品牌一款电动汽车的后座，该公司法国总监雷米·艾巴利表示，他不认为贸易障碍会阻碍极氪的雄心。 As for the Chinese companies, “you can see it as a threat, or you can see it as a chance” for Europe, he said. 他说，至于中国公司，“你可以将其视为威胁，也可以将其视为欧洲的机遇。” James Paton是时报国际商业和经济记者，常驻伦敦。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

Shut out of the United States and facing weak demand at home, they are aiming to build on their rapid gains in Europe and expand local production to stay ahead of tougher trade restrictions. 尽管欧洲努力遏制中国低成本汽车的涌入，中国公司却没有放缓脚步的迹象。它们被挡在美国之外，又面临国内需求疲软，因此正致力于巩固在欧洲的快速增长势头，并扩大当地生产，以应对日益严厉的贸易限制。 Xpeng is one example. The Chinese company is taking an “in-Europe, for-Europe” approach, He Xiaopeng, a co-founder, said in a speech on Tuesday. The company plans to focus on “localizing” production in Europe as it moves toward a target of selling about 500,000 vehicles a year in the region by 2030. Xpeng is open to sharing its technology with European companies, he said. 小鹏就是一个例子。这家中国公司的联合创始人何小鹏在周二的演讲中表示，公司正在采取“在欧洲、为欧洲”的方式。该公司计划专注于在欧洲实现“本地化”生产，朝着到2030年在该地区年销量约50万辆的目标迈进。他说，小鹏愿意与欧洲公司分享其技术。 “We want to have deeper collaboration in Europe,” he said. “我们希望在欧洲进行更深入的合作，”他说。 Anne-Laure Paulic is one potential customer. She and her family might replace their BMW — and buy their first Chinese car. Ms. Paulic, a consultant, and her husband took the train to Paris from their home in Brittany in northwest France to check out the newest models. 安娜-洛尔·波利克就是一位潜在客户。她和家人可能会换掉他们的宝马，并购买他们的第一辆中国汽车。波利克是一名顾问，她和丈夫从法国西北部布列塔尼的家中乘火车到巴黎去看最新车型。 “It’s a nice surprise,” she said as she stepped out of a gleaming Xpeng G9L, which is produced in Austria and has an array of features increasingly common in Chinese cars: a 21-inch, ceiling-mounted screen; climate-controlled seats with massage; and a refrigerator. “I love the gadgets.” “这是一个不错的惊喜，”她在走出闪亮的小鹏G9L时说道。该车在奥地利生产，配备了一系列在中国汽车中越来越常见的功能：21英寸吸顶屏幕、带按摩的温控座椅和一台冰箱。“我喜欢这些小玩意。” 小鹏汽车联合创始人何小鹏表示，该公司正采取“在欧洲、为欧洲”的策略来销售其汽车。 Spain has emerged as a prime destination for Chinese carmakers seeking partnerships with European and American rivals. Another electric car on display, Leapmotor’s B10, is produced at the Chinese company’s first European manufacturing facility, in Zaragoza, and developed with Stellantis. 西班牙已成为中国汽车制造商寻求与欧美竞争对手建立合作关系的首选目的地。展览上的另一款电动汽车零跑B10在中国公司位于萨拉戈萨的首个欧洲制造工厂生产，与斯泰兰蒂斯共同开发。 Geely is working with Ford Motor at the U.S. company’s plant in Valencia, SAIC plans to manufacture cars in Galicia and Chery has joined with a Spanish brand to produce cars in Barcelona. 吉利正与福特汽车在这家美国公司位于瓦伦西亚的工厂合作，上汽计划在加利西亚生产汽车，奇瑞已与一个西班牙品牌合作，在巴塞罗那生产汽车。 Other countries are attracting Chinese companies, too. BYD, China’s dominant maker of electric vehicles, plans to produce cars in Hungary and is considering more factories, possibly in France. The trend is set to continue as struggling European companies turn to Chinese competitors to fill underused plants. 其他国家也在吸引中国公司。中国领先的电动汽车制造商比亚迪计划在匈牙利生产汽车，并正在考虑更多工厂，可能选址在法国。随着陷入困境的欧洲公司转向中国竞争对手以填补产能利用率不足的工厂，这一趋势势必会继续。 Chinese companies are aiming to produce more cars in Europe as the region’s policymakers try to curtail their exports. European Union officials said a deal with Beijing on Friday could halve the number of Chinese hybrid cars sent to the bloc in the next four years, helping to alleviate pressure on the European car industry. Officials are also discussing proposed rules that would prioritize European companies when public money is at stake. 中国公司正寻求在欧洲生产更多汽车，而欧洲政策制定者试图限制中国公司的出口。欧盟官员表示， 周五与北京达成的一项协议 可能使中国在未来四年向欧盟出口的混合动力汽车数量减半，有助于缓解欧洲汽车工业的压力。官员们还在讨论一项拟议规则，在涉及公共资金时优先考虑欧洲公司。 France’s president, Emmanuel Macron, who visited the event on Monday, has said Europe’s industries face a “life or death” moment. 法国总统马克龙周一参观了展会，他曾表示欧洲工业正面临“生死攸关”的时刻。 巴黎车展上的零跑B03。 Still, efforts to stem the flow could be just “a temporary respite, as in the medium term we see Chinese manufacturers near-shoring more to the E.U.,” said Matthias Schmidt, an analyst in Germany. Restricting supplies could also allow Chinese companies to raise prices, benefiting those manufacturers in Europe over time. 不过，德国分析师马蒂亚斯·施密特说，遏制这股潮流的努力可能只是“暂时的喘息，因为从中期来看，我们看到中国制造商更多地向欧盟近岸外包”。限制供应也可能让中国公司 提高价格 ，随着时间推移，这会使它们在欧洲的制造商受益。 China’s rise is a new chapter for the Paris show, first held at the Jardin des Tuileries in 1898. Although companies such as Renault are keen to demonstrate their prowess, one prominent European company — BMW — opted not to attend. 中国的崛起是巴黎车展的新篇章。该车展于1898年首次在杜乐丽花园举办。此次尽管雷诺等公司急于展示其实力，但一家知名的欧洲公司——宝马——此次却选择缺席。 Chinese companies “have a big foot in the door,” said Serge Gachot, the director of the event and a former executive at Toyota and other companies. “They are very disruptive and fast moving.” 车展总监、曾任丰田等公司高管的塞尔日·加肖说，中国公司“已经一只脚牢牢踏进门内”。“它们极具颠覆性，而且行动迅速。” BYD’s sales in Europe have more than doubled this year, while sales of Chery and Leapmotor have grown at an even faster clip. After selling 700,000 cars back home, Xiaomi sees Germany as the foundation of its European expansion plans. 比亚迪今年在欧洲的销量增长了一倍多，奇瑞和零跑的销量增长更快。在中国本土售出70万辆汽车后，小米将德国视为其欧洲扩张计划的基础。 Chinese cars already account for about one in every 10 cars sold in Europe. And by teaming up with Chinese companies to keep their factories running, European manufacturers could end up helping their rivals. Yet they may have little choice but to cooperate and learn from their Chinese counterparts, said Ferdinand Dudenhöffer, an analyst and former industry executive. 中国汽车目前已占欧洲汽车销量的约十分之一。而欧洲制造商若为了维持工厂运转而与中国企业合作，最终可能会助长竞争对手的势头。但分析师、前行业高管费迪南德·杜登赫费尔说，它们可能别无选择，只能合作，并向中国同行学习。 “You can’t stand alone,” he said. “你不能单打独斗，”他说。 One of Zeekr’s mottos, “the power of a giant and a European soul,” is emblazoned on the wall of its exhibit. Sitting in the back of one of the Geely brand’s electric cars, its director in France, Rémy Aybaly, said he did not expect trade hurdles to hamper Zeekr’s ambitions. 极氪的口号之一“巨人的力量与欧洲的灵魂”醒目地展示在其展台墙上。坐在吉利品牌一款电动汽车的后座，该公司法国总监雷米·艾巴利表示，他不认为贸易障碍会阻碍极氪的雄心。 As for the Chinese companies, “you can see it as a threat, or you can see it as a chance” for Europe, he said. 他说，至于中国公司，“你可以将其视为威胁，也可以将其视为欧洲的机遇。” James Paton 是时报国际商业和经济记者，常驻伦敦。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 揭秘俄罗斯鼠疫研究所：系统庞大隐秘，安全防护存疑
description: K. R. CALLAWAY2026年10月16日伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所发布的一张照片，显示2019年专家们在俄罗斯克拉斯诺亚尔斯克的一间实验室里工作。 Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute, via Agence France-Presse — Getty Images Nearly two weeks after a 28-year-old researcher died from a mysterious infection while working in a Russian plague research laboratory, health officials around the world are still waiting for answers. 近两周前，一名在俄罗斯鼠疫研究实验室工作的28岁研究员因不明感染死亡，世界各地的卫生官员至今仍在等待答案。 Darya Shipilova, a lab worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute, was initially reported to have contracted pneumonic plague, raising concerns about the kinds of research being conducted at the facility and the safety measures employed there. 达里娅·希皮洛娃是伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所的一名实验室工作人员。最初有报道称她感染了肺鼠疫，这引发了人们对这家机构正在进行的研究种类及其安全措施的担忧。 The Russian authorities have since ruled out pneumonic plague, a bacterial infection caused by the same pathogen as the better known bubonic plague, as the cause of Ms. Shipilova’s death, but have yet to confirm which pathogen was responsible for causing her pneumonia. 此后，俄罗斯当局排除了肺鼠疫是希皮洛娃死因的可能性，但尚未确认导致她患上肺炎的病原体是什么。肺鼠疫是一种细菌感染，由与更为人熟知的腺鼠疫相同的病原体引起。 The incident, which led to denunciations by the United States and other governments, has exposed the international community’s lingering mistrust of Russian biomedical research, which harks back to the Soviet military’s once-robust programs for developing biological weapons. 这起事件引发美国及他国政府的谴责，也暴露出国际社会对俄罗斯生物医学研究挥之不去的怀疑。这种不信任可以追溯到苏联军方当年强大的生物武器研发计划。 The institute in Irkutsk never functioned as a military facility, but it was part of the broad yet secretive “Anti-Plague System.” At hundreds of field sites and labs across the Soviet Union, thousands of researchers were responsible for tracking emerging strains of plague and other endemic diseases, exterminating disease-causing rodents and developing vaccines. These facilities, experts said, had also provided pathogen samples to the military labs responsible for creating bioweapons during the Soviet era. 伊尔库茨克的这家研究所从未作为军事设施运作，但它是庞大而隐秘的“抗鼠疫系统”的一部分。在苏联各地的数百个野外站点和实验室中，数千名研究人员负责追踪新出现的鼠疫菌株和其他地方病，消灭致病啮齿动物并研发疫苗。专家表示，在苏联时代，这些机构还曾向负责研发生物武器的军事实验室提供病原体样本。 Most of these facilities are still functioning, and while those in Russia remain closely-guarded, some in former Soviet states have opened their doors to international researchers looking to learn about the fabled system. 这些机构大多数至今仍在运作。虽然俄罗斯境内的那些机构依然戒备森严，但一些位于前苏联加盟共和国的机构已经向国际研究人员敞开大门，让他们得以了解这个颇具传奇色彩的体系。 The Anti-Plague System 抗鼠疫系统 一张经过着色处理的鼠疫耶尔森菌扫描电子显微镜图像。这种细菌是鼠疫的病原体。 Although the Black Death of 14th-century Europe is the deadliest and best-known outbreak of the plague, a disease caused by the bacterium Y. pestis and carried by rodents, the illness has haunted Eurasia for thousands of years. 14世纪欧洲的黑死病是历史上死亡人数最多、也最为人熟知的一次鼠疫大流行，但这种由鼠疫耶尔森菌引起、通过啮齿动物传播的疾病已经困扰欧亚大陆数千年。 To put a stop to the frequent outbreaks in rural areas, where plague-harboring animals like rats, gerbils and marmots are endemic, the Soviet Union established a series of field sites and research institutes early in the 20th-century. They called it the “Anti-Plague System.” 为了遏制农村地区频繁暴发的疫情——那里广泛分布着携带鼠疫病原体的老鼠、沙鼠和旱獭等动物，苏联在20世纪初建立了一系列野外站点和研究机构，称之为“抗鼠疫系统”。 “The goal of their work was to be a central institute that surveils the vast areas around them, including the steppes that have large populations of burrowing wild rodents,” said Susan D. Jones, a veterinary historian at the University of Minnesota who in 2018 visited a former Soviet Anti-Plague Institute in what is now Kazakhstan. 明尼苏达大学研究兽医学历史的苏珊·琼斯说：“他们的目标是建立一个中心研究所，对周边广阔地区进行监测，包括穴居野生啮齿动物大量栖息的草原。”2018年，她曾参观了位于如今哈萨克斯坦境内的一家前苏联抗鼠疫研究所。 In its early days, the program was rudimentary. Scientists would venture on horseback into plague hot spots, often staying in tents or renting rooms from local residents, and would spend their days exterminating rodents, digging up their burrows and burning their food supplies in an attempt to eradicate the diseases they carried. 在早期，这项计划相当简陋。科学家骑马前往鼠疫高发地区，经常住在帐篷里，或向当地居民租房。他们每天捕杀啮齿动物，挖开这些动物的洞穴，焚烧它们的食物来源，试图消灭这些动物携带的疾病。 Many of these expeditions were conducted without effective disinfectants or personal protective equipment, making the job of Anti-Plague workers a very dangerous one. And the eradication efforts didn’t stop the spread of the disease. 许多此类考察是在没有有效消毒剂或个人防护装备的情况下进行的，这使得抗鼠疫工作人员的工作非常危险。而且灭鼠行动并未能阻止疾病传播。 Between the 1920s and 1950s, however, the program shifted its focus from eradication to outbreak prevention, opening up a series of labs in cities around the U.S.S.R. By the middle of the 20th century, as an antibiotic to treat plague was developed, thousands of year-round employees staffed these labs, with hundreds more hired seasonally to collect samples in the field. 不过，从20世纪20年代到50年代，该计划逐渐将重点从消灭鼠疫转向预防疫情暴发，并在苏联各地的城市建立了一系列实验室。到20世纪中叶，随着治疗鼠疫的抗生素问世，这些实验室已经雇用了数千名全年工作的员工，每年还会季节性雇用数百人到野外采集样本。 Inside the Soviet-Era Labs 苏联时代的实验室内部 2025年5月，西伯利亚和远东伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所的卫星照片。 The research conducted at these Soviet-era facilities was “hidden behind a curtain of secrecy,” a former anti-plague researcher, Dr. Moisey Iosifovich Levi, wrote in a 1994 essay. 前鼠疫防治研究员莫伊谢伊·约瑟福维奇·列维博士在1994年的一篇文章中写道，这些苏联时代的机构开展的研究“隐藏在保密的帷幕之后”。 To avoid links being made between their work and the bioweapon development programs in military labs, workers at the plague labs were instructed never to mention anything specific about their work in their conversations. 为了避免外界将他们的工作与军事实验室的生物武器研发计划联系起来，鼠疫实验室的工作人员接到指示，不得向他人透露工作细节。 Furthermore, the lab buildings themselves were built to look like normal housing units. Workers in many facilities maintained gardens, kept the lab windows open and walked around in normal clothing or even pajamas rather than wear white coats. 此外，实验室建筑本身也被设计成普通住宅的模样。许多机构的工作人员种植花草蔬菜，敞开实验室的窗户，穿着日常服装甚至睡衣走来走去，而不是穿白大褂。 It wasn’t until one stepped inside the lab and saw scientific equipment — refrigerators full of pathogen samples, large sterilizers boiling used equipment and long tables dotted with microscopes — that the buildings’ true purpose became apparent. 只有走进实验室，看到里面的科研设备——装满病原体样本的冰箱、对使用过的器械进行煮沸消毒的大型灭菌设备，以及摆满显微镜的长桌——人们才会发现这些建筑的真正用途。 Because of these unusual working conditions, “biosafety and biosecurity was very different from what we have in Western countries,” said Sonia Ben Ouagrham-Gormley, a biodefense researcher at George Mason University who has visited many anti-plague research institutes in former Soviet states. 乔治梅森大学的生物防御研究员索尼娅·本·瓦格拉姆-戈姆利曾参观过前苏联国家的多家抗鼠疫研究所。她说，由于这些不寻常的工作条件，“那里的生物安全和生物安保措施与我们西方国家的做法大不相同”。 In a series of anthologies entitled “Interesting Stories of the Events and People of the Anti-Plague System of Russia and the Soviet Union,” edited by Dr. Levi, authors describe dangerous conditions that included outbreaks among animals kept in the facilities, lab fires and lost pathogen samples. 在列维博士主编的一套名为《俄罗斯和苏联抗鼠疫体系人物与事件趣闻》的文集中，作者们描述了种种危险状况，包括研究机构饲养的动物暴发疫情、实验室发生火灾，以及病原体样本丢失。 In the final years of the Soviet Union, several facilities were provided with safer and more effective lab equipment. Household refrigerators were swapped for more secure versions and fume hoods replaced open windows. But funding for these changes was difficult to come by, so smaller and more remote facilities, including the institute in Irkutsk, struggled to keep up. 苏联解体前的最后几年，一些机构获得了更安全、更有效的实验室设备。家用冰箱被替换成安全性更高的型号，通风橱取代了敞开的窗户。但这些改造所需的资金难以筹措，因此规模较小、地处偏远的机构难以跟上改进的步伐，伊尔库茨克研究所也是这类机构之一。 “In recent decades, much has changed at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute, and not for the better. In contrast with other Anti-Plague institutes, it did not get attention,” wrote a former director of the institute, Igor Valerianovich Domaradsky, in an essay included in Dr. Levi’s anthologies. 伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所前所长伊戈尔·瓦列里安诺维奇·多马拉茨基在收录于列维博士文集的一篇文章中写道：“近几十年来，伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所发生了很大变化，而且不是朝着好的方向。与其他抗鼠疫研究所相比，它没有得到关注。” “Therefore, the institute greatly lagged in acquiring new equipment and technology, which could not but affect the development of the institute,” he added. “What a shame.” 他接着写道：“因此，该研究所在获取新设备和新技术方面大大落后，这不可避免地影响了研究所的发展。真是令人遗憾。” The Facilities Today 这些机构的现状 俄罗斯伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究中心外，摄于10月7日。 After the fall of the Soviet Union, most labs, from the advanced centers in wealthy cities to financially struggling rural facilities, remained open. And for decades, many were largely unchanged. 苏联解体后，从富裕城市里的先进研究中心到资金拮据的农村机构，大多数实验室都继续运作。而且许多实验室在此后几十年里基本没有变化。 Dr. Ben Ouagrham-Gormley visited over 100 former-Soviet facilities in the early 2000s, alongside colleagues from the James Martin Center for Nonproliferation Studies. They found that entering one was like stepping into the past; tracking pathogen samples was done with pen and paper, and many vials were stored in oft-opened refrigerators, with wax seals used to indicate who had last opened them. 21世纪前几年，本·瓦格拉姆-戈姆利博士与詹姆斯·马丁防扩散研究中心的同事一起，走访了100多处前苏联设施。他们发现，走进这些地方就仿佛回到了过去：病原体样本的追踪仍靠纸笔记录，许多样本瓶存放在经常打开的冰箱里，用蜡封表明谁最后打开过它们。 Many of the buildings, the researchers said, had no external security measures. And security inside was minimal, as well. 研究人员表示，许多建筑没有外部安保措施，内部的安全防护也非常有限。 “We got there for a visit, and in the lab there was a table under a window that was wide open, because it was a summer, and there’s no air conditioning, and there were piles of plague cultures on the table,” Dr. Ben Ouagrham-Gormley said of one facility. 本·瓦格拉姆-戈姆利博士在谈到其中一家机构时说：“我们去参观的时候，发现实验室里有一张桌子，就摆在一扇大开的窗户下面。因为是夏天，又没有空调，桌子上堆着一大堆鼠疫培养物。” Over the next two decades, several facilities in former Soviet states were refurbished or rebuilt to accommodate updated scientific equipment, allowing some to become state-of-the-art centers visited by researchers from around the world. 此后20年里，前苏联国家的一些机构得到翻修或重建，配备了更新的科研设备，其中一些因此成为最先进的研究中心，吸引世界各地的研究人员前来参观。 “There are levels of containment within these buildings,” Dr. Jones said of the facility that she visited in Kazakhstan in 2018. “Once one is in the most high level of containment, one will be wearing full P.P.E. and all work is done in sealed containment facilities.” 琼斯博士谈到她2018年参观的哈萨克斯坦一家研究机构时说：“这些建筑内部设有不同级别的生物防护区域。进入最高防护级别的区域后，工作人员必须穿戴全套个人防护装备，所有工作都在密闭的防护设施内进行。” Because Russia has kept its Anti-Plague System facilities closed to international researchers and government officials, it’s difficult to say for certain whether facilities in that country have improved as much as those that benefited from international aid to other states after the breakup of the Soviet Union. 由于俄罗斯一直不允许国际研究人员和他国政府官员进入其抗鼠疫体系的机构，很难确定俄罗斯境内设施的改进程度是否赶上了苏联解体后接受国际援助的其他前苏国家。 “I would assume that they have not improved much,” Dr. Ben Ouagrham-Gormley said. “But they probably had maintained their procedures of Soviet time and their methods, which were good to ensure biosafety and prevent accidents in spite of a lack of equipment.” 本·瓦格拉姆-戈姆利博士说：“我猜它们没有得到太大改善。但它们很可能保留了苏联时代的操作规程和方法。尽管缺乏设备，这些规程和方法在确保生物安全、防止事故方面还是相当有效的。” About the facility in Irkutsk, little information is publicly available. However, Russian authorities have remained adamant that Ms. Shipilova’s death was not the result of unfollowed protocols or lapses in biosecurity at the facility. 关于伊尔库茨克的这家研究所，公开信息很少。不过，俄罗斯当局始终坚称，希皮洛娃之死并非该机构未遵守操作规程或生物安保存在漏洞所致。 K. CALLAWAY 2026年10月16日 伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所发布的一张照片，显示2019年专家们在俄罗斯克拉斯诺亚尔斯克的一间实验室里工作。 Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute, via Agence France-Presse — Getty Images Nearly two weeks after a 28-year-old researcher died from a mysterious infection while working in a Russian plague research laboratory, health officials around the world are still waiting for answers. 近两周前，一名在俄罗斯鼠疫研究实验室工作的28岁研究员因不明感染死亡，世界各地的卫生官员至今仍在等待答案。 Darya Shipilova, a lab worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute, was initially reported to have contracted pneumonic plague, raising concerns about the kinds of research being conducted at the facility and the safety measures employed there. 达里娅·希皮洛娃是伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所的一名实验室工作人员。最初有报道称她感染了肺鼠疫，这引发了人们对这家机构正在进行的研究种类及其安全措施的担忧。 The Russian authorities have since ruled out pneumonic plague, a bacterial infection caused by the same pathogen as the better known bubonic plague, as the cause of Ms. Shipilova’s death, but have yet to confirm which pathogen was responsible for causing her pneumonia. 此后，俄罗斯当局排除了肺鼠疫是希皮洛娃死因的可能性，但尚未确认导致她患上肺炎的病原体是什么。肺鼠疫是一种细菌感染，由与更为人熟知的腺鼠疫相同的病原体引起。 The incident, which led to denunciations by the United States and other governments, has exposed the international community’s lingering mistrust of Russian biomedical research, which harks back to the Soviet military’s once-robust programs for developing biological weapons. 这起事件引发美国及他国政府的谴责，也暴露出国际社会对俄罗斯生物医学研究挥之不去的怀疑。这种不信任可以追溯到苏联军方当年强大的生物武器研发计划。 The institute in Irkutsk never functioned as a military facility, but it was part of the broad yet secretive “Anti-Plague System.” At hundreds of field sites and labs across the Soviet Union, thousands of researchers were responsible for tracking emerging strains of plague and other endemic diseases, exterminating disease-causing rodents and developing vaccines. These facilities, experts said, had also provided pathogen samples to the military labs responsible for creating bioweapons during the Soviet era. 伊尔库茨克的这家研究所从未作为军事设施运作，但它是庞大而隐秘的“抗鼠疫系统”的一部分。在苏联各地的数百个野外站点和实验室中，数千名研究人员负责追踪新出现的鼠疫菌株和其他地方病，消灭致病啮齿动物并研发疫苗。专家表示，在苏联时代，这些机构还曾向负责研发生物武器的军事实验室提供病原体样本。 Most of these facilities are still functioning, and while those in Russia remain closely-guarded, some in former Soviet states have opened their doors to international researchers looking to learn about the fabled system. 这些机构大多数至今仍在运作。虽然俄罗斯境内的那些机构依然戒备森严，但一些位于前苏联加盟共和国的机构已经向国际研究人员敞开大门，让他们得以了解这个颇具传奇色彩的体系。 The Anti-Plague System 抗鼠疫系统 一张经过着色处理的鼠疫耶尔森菌扫描电子显微镜图像。这种细菌是鼠疫的病原体。 Although the Black Death of 14th-century Europe is the deadliest and best-known outbreak of the plague, a disease caused by the bacterium Y. pestis and carried by rodents, the illness has haunted Eurasia for thousands of years. 14世纪欧洲的黑死病是历史上死亡人数最多、也最为人熟知的一次鼠疫大流行，但这种由鼠疫耶尔森菌引起、通过啮齿动物传播的疾病已经困扰欧亚大陆数千年。 To put a stop to the frequent outbreaks in rural areas, where plague-harboring animals like rats, gerbils and marmots are endemic, the Soviet Union established a series of field sites and research institutes early in the 20th-century. They called it the “Anti-Plague System.” 为了遏制农村地区频繁暴发的疫情——那里广泛分布着携带鼠疫病原体的老鼠、沙鼠和旱獭等动物，苏联在20世纪初建立了一系列野外站点和研究机构，称之为“抗鼠疫系统”。 “The goal of their work was to be a central institute that surveils the vast areas around them, including the steppes that have large populations of burrowing wild rodents,” said Susan D. Jones, a veterinary historian at the University of Minnesota who in 2018 visited a former Soviet Anti-Plague Institute in what is now Kazakhstan. 明尼苏达大学研究兽医学历史的苏珊·琼斯说：“他们的目标是建立一个中心研究所，对周边广阔地区进行监测，包括穴居野生啮齿动物大量栖息的草原。”2018年，她曾参观了位于如今哈萨克斯坦境内的一家前苏联抗鼠疫研究所。 In its early days, the program was rudimentary. Scientists would venture on horseback into plague hot spots, often staying in tents or renting rooms from local residents, and would spend their days exterminating rodents, digging up their burrows and burning their food supplies in an attempt to eradicate the diseases they carried. 在早期，这项计划相当简陋。科学家骑马前往鼠疫高发地区，经常住在帐篷里，或向当地居民租房。他们每天捕杀啮齿动物，挖开这些动物的洞穴，焚烧它们的食物来源，试图消灭这些动物携带的疾病。 Many of these expeditions were conducted without effective disinfectants or personal protective equipment, making the job of Anti-Plague workers a very dangerous one. And the eradication efforts didn’t stop the spread of the disease. 许多此类考察是在没有有效消毒剂或个人防护装备的情况下进行的，这使得抗鼠疫工作人员的工作非常危险。而且灭鼠行动并未能阻止疾病传播。 Between the 1920s and 1950s, however, the program shifted its focus from eradication to outbreak prevention, opening up a series of labs in cities around the U.S.S.R. Workers in many facilities maintained gardens, kept the lab windows open and walked around in normal clothing or even pajamas rather than wear white coats. 此外，实验室建筑本身也被设计成普通住宅的模样。许多机构的工作人员种植花草蔬菜，敞开实验室的窗户，穿着日常服装甚至睡衣走来走去，而不是穿白大褂。 It wasn’t until one stepped inside the lab and saw scientific equipment — refrigerators full of pathogen samples, large sterilizers boiling used equipment and long tables dotted with microscopes — that the buildings’ true purpose became apparent. 只有走进实验室，看到里面的科研设备——装满病原体样本的冰箱、对使用过的器械进行煮沸消毒的大型灭菌设备，以及摆满显微镜的长桌——人们才会发现这些建筑的真正用途。 Because of these unusual working conditions, “biosafety and biosecurity was very different from what we have in Western countries,” said Sonia Ben Ouagrham-Gormley, a biodefense researcher at George Mason University who has visited many anti-plague research institutes in former Soviet states. 乔治梅森大学的生物防御研究员索尼娅·本·瓦格拉姆-戈姆利曾参观过前苏联国家的多家抗鼠疫研究所。她说，由于这些不寻常的工作条件，“那里的生物安全和生物安保措施与我们西方国家的做法大不相同”。 In a series of anthologies entitled “Interesting Stories of the Events and People of the Anti-Plague System of Russia and the Soviet Union,” edited by Dr. Levi, authors describe dangerous conditions that included outbreaks among animals kept in the facilities, lab fires and lost pathogen samples. 在列维博士主编的一套名为《俄罗斯和苏联抗鼠疫体系人物与事件趣闻》的文集中，作者们描述了种种危险状况，包括研究机构饲养的动物暴发疫情、实验室发生火灾，以及病原体样本丢失。 In the final years of the Soviet Union, several facilities were provided with safer and more effective lab equipment. Household refrigerators were swapped for more secure versions and fume hoods replaced open windows. But funding for these changes was difficult to come by, so smaller and more remote facilities, including the institute in Irkutsk, struggled to keep up. 苏联解体前的最后几年，一些机构获得了更安全、更有效的实验室设备。家用冰箱被替换成安全性更高的型号，通风橱取代了敞开的窗户。但这些改造所需的资金难以筹措，因此规模较小、地处偏远的机构难以跟上改进的步伐，伊尔库茨克研究所也是这类机构之一。 “In recent decades, much has changed at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute, and not for the better. In contrast with other Anti-Plague institutes, it did not get attention,” wrote a former director of the institute, Igor Valerianovich Domaradsky, in an essay included in Dr. Levi’s anthologies. 伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所前所长伊戈尔·瓦列里安诺维奇·多马拉茨基在收录于列维博士文集的一篇文章中写道：“近几十年来，伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所发生了很大变化，而且不是朝着好的方向。与其他抗鼠疫研究所相比，它没有得到关注。” “Therefore, the institute greatly lagged in acquiring new equipment and technology, which could not but affect the development of the institute,” he added. “What a shame.” 他接着写道：“因此，该研究所在获取新设备和新技术方面大大落后，这不可避免地影响了研究所的发展。真是令人遗憾。” The Facilities Today 这些机构的现状 俄罗斯伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究中心外，摄于10月7日。 After the fall of the Soviet Union, most labs, from the advanced centers in wealthy cities to financially struggling rural facilities, remained open. And for decades, many were largely unchanged. 苏联解体后，从富裕城市里的先进研究中心到资金拮据的农村机构，大多数实验室都继续运作。而且许多实验室在此后几十年里基本没有变化。 Dr. Ben Ouagrham-Gormley visited over 100 former-Soviet facilities in the early 2000s, alongside colleagues from the James Martin Center for Nonproliferation Studies. title: 新鸭绿江大桥通车，中朝贸易关系升温
description: CHOE SANG-HUN2026年10月16日周四，从中国丹东眺望正式开通的新鸭绿江大桥。 Iori Sagisawa/Kyodo News, via Associated Press North Korea and China on Thursday opened the New Yalu River Bridge, the largest border crossing between the two countries, a sign of growing trade despite international sanctions aimed at constraining North Korea’s economy and nuclear weapons program. 周四，朝鲜与中国开通了两国间最大的边境通道——新鸭绿江大桥。尽管旨在遏制朝鲜经济及核武器计划的国际制裁依然存在，此举表明双边贸易正在不断增长。 In recent weeks, travelers returning from the river border reported that trucks and cars were already crossing the four-lane, nearly two-mile long bridge from China into North Korea. The bridge connects the Chinese city of Dandong to Sinuiju, a North Korean city on the Yalu River that forms much of the border between the two countries. 最近几周，从边境江段返回的旅客反映，已有卡车和客车经由这座双向四车道、长约三公里的大桥从中国驶入朝鲜。这座桥梁连接中国丹东市与坐落于鸭绿江畔的朝鲜城市新义州，鸭绿江构成了两国间的大部分边界。 Its opening, which was reported by the Chinese state media, comes just a month after North Korea and Russia inaugurated their first — and much smaller — road bridge across the Tumen River border. The consecutive bridge openings underscore Pyongyang’s deepening ties with its two main allies. 据中国官方媒体报道，这座桥梁通车距朝俄启用横跨图们江边境、规模小得多的首座公路桥仅相隔一个月。两座跨境桥梁的相继启用凸显出平壤正在深化与这两大主要盟友的关系。 In a video address at the opening ceremony, Premier Li Qiang of China said the new bridge “will not only strongly promote bilateral economic and trade cooperation but also further strengthen people-to-people exchanges,” according to Chinese state media. Prime Minister Pak Thae-song of North Korea also delivered a speech via video, it said. 据中国官方媒体报道，中国国务院总理李强在开通仪式上发表视频致辞时表示，新大桥“不仅将有力促进两国经贸合作，也将进一步密切双方人员往来”。报道称，朝鲜内阁总理朴泰成亦通过视频致辞。 Russia built its road bridge to supplement its lone rail link with North Korea after Pyongyang sent weapons and troops to aid Moscow’s war against Ukraine. As North Korea’s relationship with Russia has strengthened, China has moved to expand its own trade with Pyongyang in an effort to maintain its economic influence over its neighbor. 随着平壤向对乌克兰作战的莫斯科提供武器和军事人员援助，俄罗斯建造了公路桥，以弥补其与朝鲜间单一铁路连接的不足。随着朝俄关系不断强化，中国也着手扩大对朝贸易，力求保持对该邻国的经济影响力。 Moscow and Beijing had already weakened the international sanctions against North Korea when they worked together in 2024 to dissolve the United Nations panel responsible for monitoring the enforcement of sanctions. Both countries have also urged Washington to ease restrictions on Pyongyang, arguing that the sanctions have failed to halt the country’s nuclear weapons development. 早在2024年，莫斯科与北京联手解散了负责监督制裁执行情况的联合国专家小组，从而削弱了针对朝鲜的国际制裁。两国还敦促华盛顿放宽对朝限制，主张制裁并未能阻止朝鲜研发核武器。 Analysts warn that these new bridges could serve as a trade route for North Korea, whose economy has been strained by U.N. sanctions that prohibit key exports, including coal and labor, and severely restrict fuel imports. 分析人士警告称，这些新建桥梁可能成为朝鲜的贸易通道。受制于联合国禁止煤炭和劳工等关键出口并严控燃料进口的制裁措施，朝鲜经济此前已承受重压。 Until now, Sinuiju and Dandong were linked primarily by the 83-year-old Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, which features just a single rail line and one road lane. The aging structure could not hold trucks weighing over 20 tons and had a strict three-mile-per-hour speed limit. In 2009, China proposed building the wider New Yalu River Bridge as part of broader efforts to bring North Korea further into its economic sphere. 此前，新义州与丹东主要依靠拥有83年历史的中朝友谊桥相连，该桥仅设一条单轨铁路和一条公路。这座老化的桥梁无法承载20吨以上的货车，且需严格保持每小时约4.8公里的限速。2009年，中国提议建造桥面更宽的新鸭绿江大桥，作为将朝鲜进一步纳入自身经济辐射范围的更广泛举措之一。 Construction was completed in 2014, with China footing the bill estimated at $329 million. But the opening was delayed for 12 years, as North Korea took time building connecting roads, customs stations and supporting facilities. 该工程于2014年竣工，耗资约3.29亿美元且全额由中方承担。但因朝方耗时修建连接道路、海关检查站及配套设施，通车时间被推迟了12年。 But Pyongyang was also concerned about becoming even more dependent on China. Decades of international sanctions have left North Korea reliant on China for nearly all of its external trade. After the U.N. Security Council blacklisted North Korea’s top exports, the country’s trade deficit with China ballooned. 平壤方面也担忧对华依赖进一步加深。数十年的国际制裁使朝鲜在几乎所有对外贸易上均依赖中国；在联合国安理会将朝鲜主要出口产品列入黑名单后，该国对华贸易逆差急剧攀升。 “From North Korea’s perspective, the opening of the New Yalu River Bridge could allow Chinese goods to enter more quickly and in larger volumes, with no guarantee that North Korea could significantly increase its own exports to China,” said Kim Gyu-beom, an analyst at the Seoul-based Institute for National Security Strategy. “There is little incentive for North Korea to welcome a scenario in which its trade deficit and dependence on China continue to deepen.” 位于首尔的国家安保战略研究院分析师金奎范（音）表示：“从朝鲜的角度来看，新鸭绿江大桥的开通可能促使中国商品更快捷、更大规模地进入，却无法确保朝鲜能大幅增加对华出口。”他指出：“若贸易逆差与对华依赖持续加深，这没有理由成为朝鲜所乐见的前景。” Analysts suggested that before agreeing to open the bridge, North Korea may have sought concessions that would facilitate exports to China and create opportunities for more North Korean workers to be employed there. 分析人士指出，在同意大桥通车前，朝鲜可能争取过某些优惠条件，以便利本国对华出口，并为更多朝鲜劳工在华务工创造机会。 North Korea’s leader, Kim Jong-un, has faced the challenge of importing the Chinese raw materials and equipment needed to rebuild his economy while also raising hard currency. North Korea has largely accomplished the latter through illicit means such as smuggling, sending workers overseas, cyber operations and cryptocurrency theft. 朝鲜领导人金正恩面临着双重挑战，既要进口重建其经济所需的中国原材料和设备，又需筹集硬通货。朝鲜主要通过走私、向海外输出劳工、网络行动以及盗窃加密货币等非法手段来实现了外汇目标。 Mr. Kim pushed his country to produce more consumer goods domestically while cracking down on the smuggling of such products from China, using the Covid-19 pandemic as justification. He has also sought to reduce the chronic trade imbalance by attracting Chinese tourists to newly built coastal and mountain resorts across North Korea. 金正恩以新冠疫情为由严打自华走私消费品，同时要求国内增产此类产品。他还试图通过吸引中国游客前往朝鲜各地新建的沿海与山区度假胜地，来缓解长期的贸易失衡状况。 China accelerated its re-engagement with North Korea after Pyongyang grew closer to Moscow during the Ukraine war. China’s leader, Xi Jinping, invited both Mr. Kim and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia to a military parade in Beijing last year. Rail service between Beijing and Pyongyang, suspended during the pandemic, resumed in March, and Mr. Xi visited Pyongyang in June. 随着平壤在乌克兰战争期间向莫斯科靠拢，中国加快了与朝鲜重新接触的步伐。去年，中国领导人习近平邀请金正恩与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·V·普京出席北京的阅兵式。疫情期间暂停的京平客运列车已于3月恢复运行，习近平6月访问了平壤。 Official trade between North Korea and China reached $1.5 billion in the first half of this year, according to Chinese data, hitting its highest level since comprehensive U.N. sanctions were fully implemented in 2017. 中国官方数据显示，今年上半年朝中官方贸易额达15亿美元，创下2017年联合国全面制裁完全落地以来的最高水平。 Choe Sang-Hun是时报驻首尔首席记者，报道韩国和朝鲜新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 星盾使用受限、俄方袭击升级：乌克兰“腹背受敌”
description: CONSTANT MÉHEUT2026年10月15日周三，基辅一栋公寓楼遭袭现场，消防员正在进行灭火作业。 Evgeniy Maloletka/Associated Press Nearly five years into its fight for national survival, Ukraine has entered a moment of intense vulnerability, under growing pressure not only from Russia but also now from the United States. 在为国家生存而战近五年之后，乌克兰陷入了一个异常脆弱的时刻，不仅来自俄罗斯的压力越来越大，如今美国也在施压。 A double blow came overnight on Wednesday. 周三夜间，乌克兰接连遭受两次打击。 Ukraine said that its military, with no warning, had lost some critical access to a military version of Starlink, a pillar of its battlefield communications. Kyiv relies on the satellite internet network, known as Starshield, which is paid for by the Pentagon. That led Ukrainian officials and analysts to surmise that the restrictions had come from Washington, as President Trump is locked in his latest feud with Ukraine’s leadership. 乌克兰表示，在没有收到任何预警的情况下，乌军突然失去了对军事版星链系统部分关键功能的使用权限，而这是乌克兰战场通信的重要支柱。基辅依赖这个名为星盾的卫星互联网网络，费用由五角大楼支付。乌克兰官员和分析人士因此推测，这些限制来自华盛顿，因为特朗普总统正与乌克兰领导层陷入新一轮争执。 At the same time, Russia unleashed dozens of ballistic missiles in a broad attack on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure early Wednesday, cutting power to 600,000 people in the capital, Kyiv. It was a dark omen for a rapidly approaching winter in which Russia is gearing up to try to push Ukraine to the breaking point as Kyiv runs low on lifesaving air defenses. 与此同时，俄罗斯周三凌晨发动大规模袭击，向乌克兰能源基础设施发射了数十枚弹道导弹，导致首都基辅60万人断电。随着冬季迅速临近，这无疑是一个不祥的预兆。俄罗斯正准备在冬季进一步施压，试图将乌克兰逼至崩溃边缘，而基辅用于救命的防空力量日益薄弱。 It was unclear how long the Starshield restrictions would remain in place. Still, the Trump administration’s treatment of Ukraine has caused outrage in a country already reeling from a string of challenges. 目前尚不清楚星盾的使用限制会持续多久。不过，特朗普政府对待乌克兰的方式已经在这个接连遭受重重打击的国家激起愤怒。 Its energy system is at risk of collapse in the coming months as Russia pounds power plants and substations, trying to deprive Ukrainians of heat and water. Its economy is being pushed to the brink by Russian strikes on its ports, warehouses and steel factories. And its budget faces a multibillion-dollar gap this year and next that could leave its military severely underfunded. 随着俄罗斯不断轰炸乌克兰的发电厂和变电站，企图切断乌克兰的供暖和供水，该国能源系统在未来几个月有崩溃的风险。俄罗斯对乌克兰港口、仓库和钢铁厂的袭击正将乌克兰经济推向崩溃边缘。与此同时，乌克兰今明两年的预算面临数十亿美元的缺口，可能导致军费严重不足。 The Starshield development was interpreted in Ukraine as part of a Trump administration pressure campaign to limit Ukraine’s ability to fight. Mr. Trump is pushing Kyiv to stop attacking oil refineries so that Russia can pump more diesel onto global markets as high prices threaten the prospects of Mr. Trump’s Republican Party in the midterm elections. 在乌克兰，星盾系统遭到限制一事被解读为特朗普政府施压行动的一部分，目的是削弱乌克兰的作战能力。特朗普正敦促基辅停止袭击俄罗斯炼油厂，以便俄罗斯向全球市场供应更多柴油。目前，高油价正威胁特朗普所属共和党在中期选举中的前景。 “Clearly, this action cannot be a coincidence and is linked to the current political situation,” Serhiy Beskrestnov, a Ukrainian military expert who advises President Volodymyr Zelensky on weapons technologies, wrote on social media about the Starlink restrictions. “显然，这一行动不可能是巧合，而是与当前政治局势有关，”为泽连斯基总统提供武器技术咨询的乌克兰军事专家谢尔希·别斯克列斯特诺夫在社交媒体上评论星链限制措施时写道。 SpaceX, which operates Starlink and Starshield, and its chief executive, Elon Musk, did not respond to requests for comment. The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment. 运营星链和星盾的SpaceX及其首席执行官埃隆·马斯克均未回应置评请求。五角大楼也没有立即回应置评请求。 Ukraine was stunned to discover the Starshield restrictions, which it said caused disruptions to several combat operations. The Ukrainian military uses Starshield in part to guide its ever-growing fleets of drones, including interceptors used to down Russian drones. The restrictions, Ukrainian officials said, tied Ukraine’s hands while leaving Russia free to wage war. 乌克兰军方震惊地发现，星盾系统突然受到限制，并表示这干扰了多项作战行动。乌军使用星盾系统的一个重要用途是为规模不断扩大的无人机机队提供导航，包括用于击落俄罗斯无人机的拦截机。乌克兰官员表示，这些限制束缚了乌克兰的手脚，却让俄罗斯可以放手作战。 Perhaps nowhere was that imbalance clearer than in the Russian air assault overnight. The barrage included 39 ballistic missiles, Mr. Zelensky said. That would be the largest such salvo during the entire war, according to a New York Times data set based on Ukrainian Air Force figures. 这种不对等局面在俄罗斯夜间发动的空袭中表现得尤为明显。泽连斯基表示，这轮袭击包括39枚弹道导弹。根据《纽约时报》依据乌克兰空军数据建立的数据集，这是整场战争期间规模最大的一次弹道导弹齐射。 Even as Russia pounds Ukraine day after day, leading to some of the highest civilian death tolls seen in years of war, Kyiv says it is abiding by Mr. Trump’s demand not to strike Russian oil refineries. Its campaign against refineries, which had led to fuel shortages across Russia, made Russians feel the war as never before. 尽管俄罗斯日复一日地猛烈轰炸乌克兰，造成多年来最严重的平民伤亡，基辅表示，自己仍在遵守特朗普停止袭击俄罗斯炼油厂的要求。此前，乌克兰针对炼油厂的袭击行动导致俄罗斯各地出现燃料短缺，让俄罗斯民众以前所未有的程度感受到战争的影响。 Kyiv has said it is unfair that Russia is still attacking Ukraine’s power plants and substations. Mr. Zelensky has asserted that the strikes violate Mr. Trump’s self-declared energy cease-fire in Ukraine. The Trump administration views the cease-fire as covering only strikes on oil refineries, even though Ukraine has none that are operational. 基辅表示，俄罗斯仍在袭击乌克兰的发电厂和变电站，这有失公平。泽连斯基坚称，这些袭击违反了特朗普自行宣布的乌克兰能源停火安排。特朗普政府则认为，这项停火安排仅涵盖针对炼油厂的袭击，尽管乌克兰目前并没有仍在运营的炼油厂。 救援人员正在转移一名在基辅公寓楼袭击中受伤的居民。 Ukraine has set aside its most potent tool against Russia in part because it is worried that Mr. Trump could follow through on an apparent threat to stop providing intelligence that Kyiv needs to warn its people of incoming Russian strikes. 乌克兰搁置了它对付俄罗斯最有力的手段，部分原因是担心特朗普可能兑现其停止提供情报的威胁。基辅需要这些情报，才能向民众预警俄罗斯即将发动的袭击。 While Ukraine’s European partners have so far stepped in to patch Ukraine’s ballooning budget gaps as Russia batters the Ukrainian economy, Europe is not believed to be able to fully fill intelligence deficits if the United States were to pull back. 在俄罗斯持续打击乌克兰经济之际，乌克兰的欧洲伙伴一直在帮助填补该国不断扩大的预算缺口。但外界普遍认为，如果美国撤出，欧洲将无法完全弥补由此产生的缺口。 Ukrainian fears have been elevated over the past two days as Mr. Zelensky has reported that Ukraine did not receive early warnings about Russian missile strikes, though Mr. Trump said on Tuesday that intelligence was still being shared. 过去两天，乌克兰的担忧进一步加剧。泽连斯基报告称，乌方没有收到俄罗斯导弹袭击的预警，尽管特朗普周二表示，美国仍在与乌克兰分享情报。 The Ukrainian Air Force clarified on Wednesday that while it had received no advance warning before a Russian missile struck at about 10:40 p.m. on Tuesday, it did receive warnings related to three subsequent waves of attacks that night. Such intelligence sharing is separate from Ukraine’s use of the Starshield system. 乌克兰空军周三澄清说，虽然周二晚间10时40分左右，一枚俄罗斯导弹来袭前，乌方没有收到提前预警，但对于当晚随后发生的三波袭击，乌方确实收到了预警。这类情报共享与乌克兰使用星盾系统是两回事。 The Starshield limitations, if they continue, could hobble Ukraine’s military operations. Starshield terminals are used for nearly everything the Ukrainian Army deploys on the battlefield: the cars that carry troops and matériel, the drones that ferry food and water to soldiers at the front, and the attack drones that fly long distances to hit Russian positions. 如果星盾的使用限制持续下去，乌克兰的军事行动可能受到严重阻碍。从运送部队和物资的车辆，到向前线士兵运送食物和饮水的无人机，再到远程飞行打击俄军阵地的攻击无人机，乌军投入战场的几乎所有装备都要用到星盾终端。 The Ukrainian military uses thousands of terminals connected to Starshield, a version of the Starlink network that is harder to hack or jam. Mr. Musk said earlier this year that Starshield was “operated by the U.S. government.” 乌克兰军方使用数以千计与星盾相连的终端。星盾是星链网络的一个版本，更难被黑客攻击或干扰。马斯克今年早些时候说过，星盾由“美国政府运营”。 2023年，乌克兰顿涅茨克地区东部前线附近，一台经过伪装的星链天线。乌克兰军方使用该系统，部分用于引导其不断壮大的无人机机群。 Sasha Maslov for The New York Times Officials from Ukraine’s defense ministry said on Wednesday that, without warning, SpaceX had restricted the use of Starshield for devices traveling faster than 100 miles per hour. When the device exceeded this speed, the terminals lost connection. The officials said the ministry was in touch with the U.S. government, SpaceX and NATO partners to address the issue. 乌克兰国防部官员周三表示，SpaceX在没有事先发出任何通知的情况下，限制了星盾在移动速度超过每小时100英里（约160公里）设备上的使用。一旦设备超过这一速度，终端就会断开连接。官员们说，国防部正在与美国政府、SpaceX和北约伙伴联系，以解决这个问题。 Ukrainian soldiers said missions had been disrupted as a result. Oleksandr, an officer in the 8th Air Assault Corps, said the restrictions had mainly affected heavy bomber and fixed-wing drones targeting Russian logistical routes and positions in occupied territory. He spoke on the condition that he be identified by only his first name, in keeping with Ukrainian military rules. 乌克兰士兵表示，相关限制已经干扰了作战任务。第八空中突击军军官亚历山大说，受影响的主要是重型轰炸无人机和固定翼无人机的作战行动。这些无人机用于打击俄罗斯在乌克兰占领区的后勤补给线和军事阵地。出于乌克兰军方规定，他只允许透露名字。 Oleksandr said that if the restrictions remained in effect, Russia would be able to reopen crucial supply routes in a matter of days, and could better protect expensive equipment, including ships, from Ukrainian attacks. 亚历山大表示，如果这些限制继续实施，俄罗斯将在几天内重新打通关键补给路线，并能更有效地保护包括舰船在内的昂贵装备，免遭乌克兰的袭击。 Starshield also provides connections to the interceptor drones that Ukraine uses to shoot down the Russian attack drones known as Shaheds, especially the fast-flying jet-powered models that Russia is now launching toward Ukraine en masse, said Mr. Beskrestnov, the military-technology adviser to Mr. Zelensky. 泽连斯基的军事技术顾问别斯克列斯特诺夫表示，星盾还为乌克兰用于击落俄罗斯“见证者”攻击无人机的拦截无人机提供通信连接，特别是在应对俄罗斯如今大规模发射、飞行速度极快的喷气动力型号时。 “In effect, our partners’ actions are depriving us of one of the few ways we have to defend the country against jet-powered Shaheds,” Mr. Beskrestnov said. “实际上，我们的伙伴正在通过这些行动剥夺我们保卫国家、抵御喷气动力‘见证者’无人机的为数不多的手段之一，”别斯克列斯特诺夫说。 Ryan Mac、Carlotta Gall、Siobhán O’Grady和Maria Varenikova对本文有报道贡献。 Constant Méheut是时报记者，报道乌克兰战争。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 老龄化的欧洲，愤怒的年轻人
description: KATRIN BENNHOLD2026年10月15日周二在法国波尔多发生的一场学生抗议活动。 Christophe Archambault/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images Over the last few years we’ve seen the rise of a formidable political force: Gen Z protesters. They have toppled governments in Bangladesh, Nepal, Peru and Madagascar. They’re behind India’s largest protests in years, which so far have forced the resignation of the country’s education minister. 过去几年中，我们见证了一股强大政治力量的崛起：Z世代抗议者。他们推翻了孟加拉国、尼泊尔、秘鲁和马达加斯加的政府。他们是印度近年来最大规模抗议活动的幕后推手，这些抗议迄今已迫使该国教育部长辞职。 Now we’re witnessing protests by young people in France, who share the anger of other Gen Z protesters around the world, but not the same political power. Because unlike their contemporaries outside the West, young people in Europe are a shrinking demographic. Today my colleague Amanda Taub writes about the intense generational tensions in the West’s aging societies and why they risk becoming a vicious cycle. 如今，我们正目睹法国年轻人的抗议活动，他们与世界各地其他Z世代抗议者有着共同的愤怒，却不具备相同的政治力量。因为与西方以外的同龄人不同，欧洲的年轻人是一个正在萎缩的人口群体。今天，我的同事阿曼达·陶布撰文探讨了西方老龄化社会中激烈的世代紧张局势，以及为什么这些局势有着演变成恶性循环的风险。 A zero-sum game 零和博弈 By Amanda Taub 文/阿曼达·陶布 France may seem like a nation of perpetual protest. But if you are trying to make sense of the latest wave of demonstrations spurred on by young people angry over dilapidated schools, it might help to cast your mind back just a few years. 法国似乎是一个永远处于抗议之中的国家。但若想理解这波由年轻人对学校设施破败的愤怒引发的最新示威浪潮，回想一下几年前的情况可能会有所帮助。 Not long ago, the French took to the streets when President Emmanuel Macron raised the retirement age from 62 to 64. The outcry was so intense that the government eventually suspended the measure; France’s pensions remain one of the biggest drains on the budget of a nation with one of the highest debt levels in Europe. 不久前，当总统马克龙将退休年龄从62岁提高到64岁时，法国人走上了街头。强烈呼声如此剧烈，以至于政府最终暂停了该措施；对于这个债务水平居欧洲前列的国家而言，法国的养老金仍然是国家预算中最大的负担之一。 Today’s protesters have taken to the barricades to demand more resources for the young, while the earlier ones marched to protect resources for the old. In both cases, the protesters saw themselves in a fight with the French government; it might be equally valid to say they were — and still are — in a fight with each other. 今天的抗议者走上街头，是为了要求为年轻人提供更多资源，此前的抗议者游行则是为了保护老年人的资源。在这两种情况下，抗议者都认为自己是在与法国政府斗争；但同样可以说，他们过去和现在，都是在彼此对抗。 The dissatisfaction currently roiling Europe, from France to Spain to Britain to Belgium, is about many things: schools, housing, pensions, unemployment. But step back, and it’s also about one big thing — a generational fight over an economic pie fixed in its size by the continent’s chronic slow economic growth. 从法国到西班牙，从英国到比利时，目前席卷欧洲的不满情绪涉及许多方面：学校、住房、养老金、失业。但退一步来看，这也是一场关于一个大问题的争斗——一场围绕经济蛋糕的代际之争，而蛋糕的大小已因欧洲长期低迷的经济增长而固定不变。 ‘Gerontonomia’ “老龄治理” As Europe’s population ages, conflict may be unavoidable. Because ultimately, different generations have different economic interests, said Tim Vlandas, a professor at Oxford. 随着欧洲人口老龄化，冲突可能是不可避免的。牛津大学教授蒂姆·弗兰达斯指出，归根结底，不同的世代拥有不同的经济利益。 Young people need investments in education, a strong labor market and affordable housing. People over 65, by contrast, tend to want generous pensions and social care, protection for the value of their homes and other assets, and low inflation, even at the cost of higher unemployment. (No one likes inflation, but retirees who rely on savings and fixed incomes are particularly sensitive to it.) 年轻人需要对教育的投资、强劲的劳动力市场和负担得起的住房。相比之下，65岁以上的人群往往希望获得丰厚的养老金和社会护理，希望其房产及其他资产的价值得到保障，并希望通胀率保持较低水平，即使这意味着失业率会上升。（没有人喜欢通胀，但依赖储蓄和固定收入的退休人员对此尤为敏感。） As older people become a larger portion of the population in aging societies, their political influence has also grown, and they have been getting their way. The result is what Vlandas calls “gerontonomia,” a form of “democratically sustained economic stagnation.” 随着老年人在老龄化社会中占总人口的比例越来越大，他们的政治影响力也随之增长，并且逐渐如愿以偿。其结果就是弗兰达斯所说的“老龄治理”，一种“由民主维持的经济停滞”形式。 The disease and its symptoms are widespread. In France, youth unemployment stands at around 20 percent. GDP growth fell to zero percent in the second quarter of this year. Pension costs make up approximately a quarter of all public spending, in part because the retirement age is so low, but there is little political appetite for changing it. Many, particularly on the left, have argued that it is possible to preserve pensions and increase education spending. But the question of how to pay remains. The looming threat of a debt crisis makes further borrowing difficult. And wealth taxes, while often politically appealing, have not raised much money in the past. 这种疾病及其症状非常普遍。在法国，青年失业率保持在20%左右。今年第二季度GDP增长降至零。养老金成本约占所有公共支出的四分之一，部分原因是退休年龄太低，但在政治上几乎没有改变它的意愿。许多人——尤其是左翼人士——主张既可以保留养老金，又可以增加教育支出。但资金来源的问题依然存在。迫在眉睫的债务危机威胁使得进一步借贷变得困难。而财富税虽然在政治上常常具有吸引力，但在过去并没有筹集到多少资金。 87岁的退休老人玛丽卡门·阿巴斯卡尔，她被驱逐出家门一事在西班牙引发了全国范围的抗议活动。 Oscar Del Pozo/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images The situation is similar in Spain, which has one of the oldest populations in Europe, and where protests over a housing crisis recently contributed to Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s decision to call new elections. While the face of the protests was an 87-year-old renter, many young people joined, because the housing crisis disproportionately affects them. 西班牙的情况也类似，该国是欧洲人口老龄化最严重的国家之一，最近针对住房危机的抗议活动促使首相桑切斯决定举行新的大选。虽然抗议活动的代表人物是一位87岁的租户，但许多年轻人也加入其中，因为住房危机对他们的影响尤为严重。 Spanish youth unemployment is over 22 percent. House prices have risen far more quickly than wages, adding to the wealth of older generations, but leaving many young people with a choice of living with their parents well into their 30s or sacrificing savings to pay a steep rent. 西班牙的青年失业率超过22%。房价上涨速度远快于工资增长，增加了年长一代的财富，却让许多年轻人面临选择：要么30多岁了还要和父母同住，要么牺牲储蓄去支付高昂的租金。 In Britain, the youth unemployment rate is lower, around 16 percent. But housing costs are steep, particularly in and around London, where most job growth is located. And the country has committed to the so-called “triple lock,” a policy that has for years ensured pensions have risen faster than wages. 在英国，青年失业率较低，约为16%。但住房成本高昂，尤其是在大部分就业增长所在的伦敦及其周边地区。此外，该国还承诺实行所谓的“三重保障”政策，该政策多年来一直确保养老金的涨幅高于工资的涨幅。 In a recent speech, Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to overhaul the policy, long considered untouchable. One union leader called the pledge “almost electoral insanity,” even though Burnham promised to spend the money saved on adult social care, which would largely benefit the aged, too. 在最近的一次演讲中，首相伯纳姆承诺改革这项长期以来被视为不可触碰的政策。一位工会领导人称这一承诺“几乎是选举上的疯狂行为”，尽管伯纳姆承诺将省下来的资金用于成人社会护理，而这大部分也将让老年人受益。 昨天，巴黎举行了一场要求实行与通胀挂钩的养老金的抗议活动。 Mehdi Fedouach/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images Why older people have an edge 为何老年人占据优势 Wealthy nations can look forward to more of these battles, but older people may continue to set the political agenda. 可以预见，富裕国家未来还会有更多这样的斗争，但老年人或将继续主导政治议程。 The elderly are well-placed to rally others to their cause, because they have institutions on their side, said Kevin Arceneaux, a political science professor at Sciences Po in Paris. Political parties and unions have an incentive to protect the interests of older people, who make up the bulk of their membership and voting coalitions. 巴黎政治学院的政治学教授凯文·阿塞诺表示，老年人非常擅长团结其他人支持他们的主张，因为他们有体制作为后盾。政党和工会有动力去保护老年人的利益，因为老年人构成了其成员和投票联盟的主体。 It is also easier to convince young people to support old-age benefits that they might one day receive than it is to convince old people to pay more for education that they will never use themselves. Younger generations share some of the benefits from spending on the elderly, experts say. Adult children still living at home may see pension payments as part of their household’s income, rather than a transfer from young workers to retirees. 此外，相比说服老年人为他们自己永远用不到的教育多掏钱，说服年轻人支持他们有朝一日可能领取的晚年福利也要容易得多。专家表示，年轻一代能分享到针对老年人支出的一些好处。仍与父母同住的成年子女可能会将养老金视为其家庭收入的一部分，而非年轻劳动者向退休人员转移的资金。 In Britain, Laura Serra, a researcher at the London School of Economics, has found that working-age generations often worry they will have to support their aging parents themselves if pensions are cut. In fact, France’s young people were out in force to support the 2023 protests against Macron’s proposed pension reform. 在英国，伦敦政治经济学院的研究员劳拉·塞拉发现，适龄劳动力世代常常担心，如果养老金被削减，他们将不得不亲自赡养老龄父母。事实上，法国的年轻人曾大举出动，支持2023年反对马克龙提出的养老金改革方案的抗议活动。 But with economic growth slow in much of the continent, and government borrowing becoming prohibitively expensive, choices may have to be made. And when they are, young people, and perhaps economies as a whole, will be at a disadvantage. 然而，由于欧洲大部分地区的经济增长缓慢，且政府借贷变得昂贵至极，人们可能不得不做出选择。一旦做出选择时，年轻人——甚至可能是整个经济体——将处于不利地位。 Last week, as young people blocked schools across the country, France’s lawmakers met to review next year’s budget. One of their first moves was to preserve a tax break for pensioners. 上周，就在年轻人封锁全国各地的学校时，法国议员们正开会审查明年的预算。他们的首批举措之一就是保留针对退休人员的税收优惠政策。 本文节译自时报全球新闻电邮The World。 翻译：晋其角

In fact, France’s young people were out in force to support the 2023 protests against Macron’s proposed pension reform. 在英国，伦敦政治经济学院的研究员劳拉·塞拉发现，适龄劳动力世代常常担心，如果养老金被削减，他们将不得不亲自赡养老龄父母。事实上，法国的年轻人曾大举出动，支持2023年反对马克龙提出的养老金改革方案的抗议活动。 But with economic growth slow in much of the continent, and government borrowing becoming prohibitively expensive, choices may have to be made. And when they are, young people, and perhaps economies as a whole, will be at a disadvantage. 然而，由于欧洲大部分地区的经济增长缓慢，且政府借贷变得昂贵至极，人们可能不得不做出选择。一旦做出选择时，年轻人——甚至可能是整个经济体——将处于不利地位。 Last week, as young people blocked schools across the country, France’s lawmakers met to review next year’s budget. One of their first moves was to preserve a tax break for pensioners . 上周，就在年轻人封锁全国各地的学校时，法国议员们正开会审查明年的预算。他们的首批举措之一就是 保留针对退休人员的税收优惠政策 。 本文节译自时报全球新闻电邮 The World 。 翻译：晋其角

title: 新任白宫新闻秘书在中国做过律师吗？我们进行了事实核查
description: SHAWN McCREESH2026年10月15日 Is President Trump’s new press secretary a lawyer — or did she just play one on TV? 特朗普总统的新任新闻秘书是一名真正的律师，还是只是在电视上演过律师？ Three days into her job, Katie Zacharia is facing questions about whether she has embroidered her credentials. She describes herself as a lawyer, and the president called her “an attorney.” When she was asked on Tuesday in which state she passed the bar exam, she twice replied, “When I moved to China.” 上任仅三天，凯蒂·扎卡里亚便面临了履历造假的质疑。她自称是lawyer（律师），而总统则称其为“an attorney”（一位执业律师）。周二，当被问及她在哪个州通过了律师资格考试时，她两次回答称：“我搬去中国的时候。” Huh? 啊？ The moment capped off a shaky debut for the woman who has accepted what is perhaps the most challenging public relations post in the United States. Now she was struggling to tell her own story. 对这位接下了或许是全美最具挑战性的公关职位的女性而言，这一幕为她波折不断的首次亮相画上了句点。如今，她正竭力把自己的经历讲圆。 On Wednesday evening, she told The New York Times that this whole mishegas over “lawyer,” “attorney,” and “China,” has been one big misunderstanding. 周三晚间，她对《纽约时报》表示，围绕“lawyer”、“attorney”与“中国”的这场纷扰完全是一场大误会。 “I assumed the question was, ‘Where were you after law school?’” she said, taking a quick phone call on the tarmac in Arizona, where the president was holding a midterm rally. “我当时以为问题是：‘你从法学院毕业后去了哪里？’”她说。当时总统正在亚利桑那州举行中期选举集会，她是在停机坪上匆匆接通电话时作出这番回应的。 “That’s all I could hear over the sound of Marine One,” she said. “And, wanting to respect protocol, the distance behind the president, kept me from moving closer to hear the question.” “在‘海军陆战队一号’的噪音下，我只能听清这些，”她说.“而且出于遵守礼宾规程的考虑，我与总统保持着一定距离，这让我无法靠前听清问题。” It was only her second day on the job, she pointed out. 她强调，那天只是她履新的第二天。 So here’s the truth about Katie Zacharia, not-quite attorney-at-law: She graduated with a law degree from Pepperdine University in 2011. That technically makes her a lawyer. But is she an attorney, someone who is licensed to practice law and give legal advice? For that, she would have needed to pass the bar. The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that she sat for the California bar exam after graduating law school, but didn’t pass. The Times was unable to find a law license for her in California, or anywhere else she has lived in the United States. 那么，关于这位算不上真正的“attorney”的凯蒂·扎卡里亚，事实究竟是怎样的：她于2011年毕业于佩珀代因大学并获法学学位。严格意义上讲，这确实使她成了一名“lawyer”。但她是否是一名拥有执业许可、能够提供法律咨询的“attorney”？若想具备这一资格，她必须通过律师资格考试。《华尔街日报》周三报道称，她在法学院毕业后曾参加加州律师资格考试，但并未通过。《纽约时报》也未能在加州或她在美居住过的任何其他地方查到其律师执业执照。 During the brief phone call Wednesday, The Times did not get a chance to press her again about whether she had ever passed a bar exam. But before she had to go, she did explain that when she first began appearing on cable news, she consulted with Pepperdine’s president as to how she should identify herself. She said she was warned not to use the words “attorney” or “esquire,” but that “lawyer” was OK. 在周三那通简短的通话中，《纽约时报》未能再次追问她是否曾通过任何律师资格考试。但在挂断前，她确实解释称，当初刚开始在有线电视新闻亮相时，她曾就该如何标明自己的身份咨询过佩珀代因大学校长。她表示，当时对方告诫她不要使用“attorney”或“esquire”这类称谓，但表示使用“lawyer”没有问题。 But what about “general counsel,” would that be OK? Because, on LinkedIn, Ms. Zacharia identified herself as such for Fix California, a group led by Trump loyalist Richard Grenell. 但使用“总法律顾问”(general counsel)又是否合规呢？因为在领英上，扎卡里亚在特朗普亲信理查德·格雷内尔领导的团体“修复加州”名下，将自己的职务标注为总法律顾问。 “You can’t be a general counsel to a company in the United States unless you’re admitted to the bar to practice law,” said Erwin Chemerinsky, the dean of the law school at the University of California, Berkeley. “A general counsel implies that you’re practicing law, giving legal advice to the company. You can’t practice law without a license.” “在美国，你要获得律师资格并获准执业，否则不得担任企业的总法律顾问，”加州大学伯克利分校法学院院长埃尔温·切梅林斯基指出，“‘总法律顾问’意味着你正在从事法律执业工作，正在为企业提供法律建议。没有执照是不得从事法律执业的。” On Wednesday, a watchdog group filed a complaint with the California State Bar Association, calling for an investigation into whether Ms. Zacharia “repeatedly held herself out to the public as entitled to practice law without a license to do so, conduct California law treats as a crime.” 周三，一家监督机构向加州律师公会递交申诉，要求调查扎卡里亚是否存在“在未获执照的情况下，屡次向公众声称自己有法律执业资质，而加州法律将这种行为视为犯罪”。 And that brings us to China. 这就牵涉到了中国之行。 The White House explained this week that Ms. Zacharia moved to China with her husband, Tyler, who had a job at a U.S. private equity firm. While there, she worked on “international transaction law,” Ms. Zacharia has claimed. 白宫本周解释称，扎卡里亚是随丈夫泰勒前往中国的，后者当时在一家美国私募股权机构任职。扎卡里亚声称，在中国期间，她从事的是“国际交易法”业务。 On her LinkedIn profile, she listed nearly two years of employment at Zhong Lun Law Firm, which is one of China’s biggest law firms, with headquarters in Beijing and offices in Tokyo, New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco and Almaty, Kazakhstan. 在其领英个人主页上，她列出了在中伦律师事务所近两年的工作经历。中伦是中国最大的律师事务所之一，总部设在北京，并在东京、纽约、洛杉矶、旧金山以及哈萨克斯坦阿拉木图设有分所。 The law firm did not respond to a request for comment on Wednesday. 该律所周三未回应置评请求。 Opportunities for foreign lawyers in China are extremely narrow. Foreign nationals cannot sit for China’s bar exam, hold a Chinese lawyer’s license or advise on Chinese law. They can, however, be hired by Chinese law firms to work on cross-border deals and to advise on foreign or international law. 外国律师在中国的执业空间极为狭窄。外国公民不得参加中国的司法考试、不得持有中国律师执业执照，也不得就中国法律提供咨询意见。不过，他们可受聘于中国律所参与跨境交易，并就外国法或国际法提供法律意见。 Gary Gao, a partner at Zhong Lun who is based in Shanghai, said the firm often hired foreigners for language assistance and to help Chinese staff understand foreign business culture. 中伦律师事务所常驻上海的合伙人高俊表示，律所经常聘用外籍人员协助语言沟通，并帮助中国员工理解外国商业文化。 “They are not practicing Chinese law at any time,” he said, adding that Ms. Zacharia’s role at the firm would have likely been similar to a paid internship. “他们在任何时候都不具备中国法律执业资格，”他表示，并补充称扎卡里亚在律所的岗位很可能类似于带薪实习。 Sida Liu, a law professor at the University of Hong Kong who specializes in mainland law, said that it is misleading for Ms. Zacharia to describe herself as a former associate at Zhong Lun, because it implies that she was a licensed lawyer in China. 专门研究内地法律的香港大学法学教授刘思达指出，扎卡里亚将自己称为中伦律所前“associate”（律师）具有误导性，因为这暗示了她曾是在中国的持证律师。 “Chinese law firms can hire foreign nationals to work in their mainland offices, but such individuals are not classified as P.R.C. lawyers because P.R.C. lawyer qualification requires P.R.C. citizenship,” Mr. Liu said, referring to the People’s Republic of China. “The title ‘associate’ may therefore be somewhat controversial.” “中国律所可以聘用外籍人士在其内地办公室工作，但这类人员不会被归类为中国律师，因为取得中国律师执业资格必须具备中国国籍，”刘思达说，“因此，使用‘associate’这一头衔可能存在争议。” So what are we to make of all this? 那么，这一切到底说明了什么？ It was Mr. Trump who called Ms. Zacharia an “attorney,” and she certainly never corrected the record. She called herself “general counsel,” which was misleading at best. 特朗普称扎卡里亚为“attorney”，而她显然从未对此进行澄清。她还自称为“总法律顾问”，这至少是一种误导。 Confucius wrote in The Analects that without the trust of the people, the state cannot stand. The same goes for a White House press secretary. It is a job that’s all about credibility. It’s pretty tough to succeed if the public (let alone the fourth estate) feels that it cannot trust what it is being told. 孔子在《论语》中写道：“民无信不立。”对于白宫新闻秘书而言亦是如此。这是一份完全建立在公信力之上的工作。如果公众（更不用说媒体界了）觉得所听到的内容不可信，那就很难做好这项工作。 Kitty Bennett自华盛顿、David Pierson自香港对本文有报道贡献。 Shawn McCreesh是《纽约时报》白宫记者，报道特朗普总统及其政府新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
